title: Minimum Absolute Difference
spaceBreakdown:
- sort(): modifies arr in place, introsort stack O(log n) - counted as O(1) per in-place convention
- res (returned vector): not counted (output)
- not counted: input arr
approach: Sort the array so that the minimum absolute difference must occur between some pair of consecutive elements (for any a ≤ b ≤ c, |b−a| ≤ |c−a|). After sorting, do one pass to find the minimum consecutive gap, then a second pass to collect every consecutive pair whose gap equals that minimum. The pairs are naturally produced in ascending order because we scan the sorted array left to right.
hints: With n up to 10^5, comparing all pairs is too slow. For any three numbers where a ≤ b ≤ c, how does the gap |b − a| relate to |c − a|?
Sort the array, then scan consecutive pairs. For [4,2,1,3], sorting gives [1,2,3,4]; consecutive gaps are all 1, so the answer is [[1,2],[2,3],[3,4]].

```
sort arr
minDiff = infinity
for i from 1 to n-1:
    minDiff = min(minDiff, arr[i] - arr[i-1])
result = []
for i from 1 to n-1:
    if arr[i] - arr[i-1] == minDiff:
        result.append([arr[i-1], arr[i]])
return result
```

**Smallest input (n=2)** - only one pair exists
`Input: arr = [5,1]` → `Expected: [[1,5]]`
⚠️ Bug: initializing minDiff to 0 instead of INT_MAX → no pair matches diff 0 → returns []

**Multiple valid answers (ties)** - several pairs share the minimum difference
`Input: arr = [4,2,1,3]` → `Expected: [[1,2],[2,3],[3,4]]`
⚠️ Bug: breaking after the first pair with minDiff → returns [[1,2]]

**Negatives mixed with positives** - values cross zero, unsorted
`Input: arr = [3,8,-10,23,19,-4,-14,27]` → `Expected: [[-14,-10],[19,23],[23,27]]`
⚠️ Bug: skipping the sort step, scanning original order → minDiff=4 from |19−23|, returns [[23,19]] (wrong order, missing two pairs)

**Minimum at the last pair** - off-by-one loop bound
`Input: arr = [1,5,10,15,19]` → `Expected: [[1,5],[15,19]]`
⚠️ Bug: loop condition i < n−1 instead of i < n → misses last gap, returns [[1,5]]

followUps.q: Instead of the minimum difference, find the k-th smallest absolute difference among all pairs.
followUps.a: Sort the array, then binary search on the answer value. For a candidate d, use two pointers on the sorted array to count pairs with difference ≤ d. TC: O(n log n + n log(max_diff)), SC: O(1).

followUps.q: Elements arrive one at a time in a stream; maintain the current minimum difference and its pairs after each insertion.
followUps.a: Keep a balanced BST (std::set). On each insert, look up the predecessor and successor to compute new candidate gaps, updating the global minimum. TC: O(n log n), SC: O(n).

followUps.q: Find all pairs with absolute difference exactly equal to a given target d (not necessarily the minimum).
followUps.a: Sort the array, then use two pointers: for each left index, advance the right index until arr[right] − arr[left] ≥ d, collecting pairs when equal. TC: O(n log n), SC: O(1).
